title: APEX 1.1 Deep Learning Discovers Archaeasins—A New Domain-of-Life Class of Antibiotics
whyItMatters: Mines 233 archaeal proteomes to uncover 12,623 archaeasins—an untapped domain of life for antibiotics—with 93% of 80 synthesized peptides killing superbugs and archaeasin-73 matching polymyxin B in mice.
summary: University of Pennsylvania researchers led by César de la Fuente-Núñez deployed APEX 1.1, a deep learning antimicrobial-peptide discovery model, to systematically mine 233 archaeal proteomes—opening the entire Archaea domain of life as a new source of antibiotics. APEX 1.1 identified 12,623 candidate molecules ("archaeasins") with distinct amino-acid compositions and cytoplasmic-membrane depolarization mechanisms; 93% of 80 synthesized archaeasins killed multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens in vitro, and lead candidate archaeasin-73 significantly reduced Acinetobacter baumannii infection loads in mice at efficacy comparable to polymyxin B.
technicalHighlights: Systematically mined 233 archaeal proteomes with APEX 1.1, identifying 12,623 novel candidate antimicrobial peptides ("archaeasins").
93% of 80 chemically synthesized archaeasins demonstrated in vitro activity against clinically critical ESKAPE pathogens.
In vivo lead archaeasin-73 cleared Acinetobacter baumannii in mouse infection models comparably to last-resort antibiotic polymyxin B.
caveats: Results are preclinical (in vitro and mouse infection models); systemic toxicity, stability, and clinical efficacy in humans remain to be evaluated.

scoreRationale.foundational: Unlocks the previously untapped Archaea domain of life as a rich structural reservoir of antibiotics with distinct membrane-depolarization action.
scoreRationale.ripple: Expands AI-driven molecular bioprospecting beyond bacteria and fungi to combat global antimicrobial resistance.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature Microbiology (2025) with 80 synthesized peptides (93% hit rate) and in vivo mouse efficacy vs. polymyxin B.
scoreRationale.velocity: Screened 233 extremophile proteomes computationally to achieve a 93% wet-lab validation rate.
